notes.title: New patch, new price!
notes.notes:
[h3]Patch 1.10 - Monday, May 1st, 2023[/h3]

[list]
[*]Added full controller support (tested with an Xbox controller).
[*]Powerups are now displayed directly on the HUD, so you can cycle through them and use them without needing to open the inventory window.
[*]Keys are now also displayed directly on the HUD.
[*]Automap is now an overlay (can be toggled via TAB key by default).
[*]Added an option for center weapon placement. This is now the default setting but you can still switch to the old right-hand view in the settings menu.
[*]Improved UI scaling at 1440p and 4K.
[*]Added full keyboard support in menu.
[*]The HUD and the automap are now available in Masochistic mode.
[*]Inventory window has been removed.
[/list]

We have good news! Gorescript made it to the Top 100 finalists for the IndieDB Game of the Year Award.

You can vote for us by clicking the image above, selecting the First Person Shooter Category and then Vote on Gorescript.

We also got three nominations in the Romanian Game Awards organized by RoGa News. Gorescript is a nominee in the Game of the Year, Best PC Game and Best Gameplay categories.

18th of March: We started the Steam Greenlight Campaign
30th of March: Gorescript was greenlit with 67% ”Yes” votes
24th of April: Gorescript’s Steam page launched
26th of April: Gorescript Open Beta
17th of May: Official launch announcement

9th of December: Gorescript entered the Top 100 finalists for IndieDB’s Game of The Year Award

http://www.indiedb.com/games/gorescript2

and help us be among the chosen titles for this award.

notes.title: Level Editor Update
notes.notes:
[img]https://i.imgur.com/pAGK6X5.gif[/img]
[h1]As promised, the Level Editor for Gorescript is now live![/h1]

The Level Editor allows you to create custom levels for Gorescript. You can:
[list]
[*] Create entirely new levels and share them on Steam Workshop
[*] Add monsters, weapons, powerups and explosive barrels
[*] Add switches, trap doors and elevators
[*] Modify lighting
[*] Script various parts of the level using Lua
[/list]
The editor is a separate app from the game itself, built as a JavaScript desktop application using GitHub’s Electron.


[h1]Mouse and keyboard controls[/h1]
Here’s a listing of the primary mouse and keyboard controls for the editor.

[b]Mouse:[/b]
[list]
[*]Left-click and hold to select/draw (depending on the currently selected layer and mode)
[*]Right-click and hold to move around
[/list]
[b]Keyboard:[/b]
[list]
[*]Hold left CTRL to append/deselect an element when multi-selecting
[*]Hold left SHIFT when drawing segments to draw them at 90 degree angles
[/list]

[b]Tutorial videos[/b]

The level editor might seem a bit scary at first, so we prepared some videos showing you how to build a simple Gorescript level. Since there’s never enough E1M1 tribute levels out there, here’s our take on the subject.

[h1]Setup, Segments and Sectors[/h1]
https://youtu.be/Copo_nO9aws
In this part we go over installing the level editor from Steam and making your first room.

Levels in Gorescript are 2.5D, meaning you can never have one room over another one. Similarly, you can’t build actual bridges (the type where you can walk above and below them). Think of a level as a blueprint for one single floor of a house.

[b]We’ve detailed how to install the editor step by step right here:[/b]
[list]
[*]Step 1 – Go to the Library – Tools menu
[*]Step 2 – Search for “Gorescript Level Editor”
[*]Step 3 – Click to install
[*]Step 4 - Start the Level Editor
[/list]

[b]The usual steps for building a room are:[/b]
[list]
[*]Draw polygons using segments
[*]Go through each polygon and convert it to a sector
[*]Go through each sector and modify properties such as floor height, floor-ceiling distance, light level, light color, etc.
[*]Mark certain sectors as doors
[*]Add lights
[/list] 

[h1]Here you can find the full tutorial on how to build nightmare fueled levels in Gorescript.[/h1]
[b][url=http://cdn.edgecast.steamstatic.com/steam/apps/618690/manuals/Gorescript_Level_Editor_Help__Reference.pdf?t=1505727223]Gorescript Level Editor Help & Reference[/url][/b]

[h1]Limitations[/h1]
[list]
[*]Only individual custom levels can be created and published. There’s no option to create and publish campaigns at this time.
[*]Since only individual custom levels can be played, there’s no “Permadeath” option when playing one.
[*]Your inventory and all random powerups are reset every time you die and respawn.
[/list]
[h1]Since we know your creativity knows no bounds send us your levels and we’ll make sure to get the word out![/h1]

notes.title: Shooter and more
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/7AUuGbX.gif[/img]

Gorescript is a classic FPS and some people, including us, would swear by that. However within the game the developer snuck some game elements that might change a bit your perspective.

Some areas in Gorescript’s levels seem like a platformer. Besides moving and shooting you need to tune your reflexes to move around with precision.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/MjXeBiY.gif[/img]

Some of the platformer areas make use of the “Strafe run” mechanic and if you manage to master that several goodies in the form of weapons and power-ups await you at the end.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/fAZiQQk.gif[/img]

For the fans of roguelike elements we have the permadeath mode. This is a high risk high gain game mode. Your score will increase and we have several achievements linked to this but at the same time, you need to be tough, pick yourself up and literally enjoy seeing the “You Died” screen followed by a new game start from the 1st level.

[img]http://i.imgur.com/lrtuTG9.gif[/img]

And finally you should be able to identify some survival horror elements in the Blackout mode. Your ammo is more precious since you’ll need it for lighting as well, making running for your life a very valid strategy, the darkened halls may get confusing and the special trigger events, unveiling monsters behind you come with an extra shot of adrenaline.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_9-Id1011Go

notes.title: Words from the press
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/Z2OsPYC.gif[/img]

More than a month passed since the launch and it’s time to go through Gorescript’s press mentions. We were extremely pleased to see a lot of players and reviewers felt the same way we did about the game and identified the elements that we thought were the strong points of Gorescript.

Of course their feedback was valuable and we also managed to see some game elements are either not that strong or they require some tweaks to make them better.

[img]http://media.indiedb.com/images/members/3/2595/2594235/profile/q3.png[/img]

PC Gamer caught on our intention to capture the classic feel of the old FPSs and obviously we’re glad they placed Gorescript in this special category.

[img]http://media.indiedb.com/images/members/3/2595/2594235/profile/q2.png[/img]

Gorescript, through its early embodiment Gorescript Classic, started as a project that meant to recapture the feeling of Doom. Sergiu, the developer of Gorescript, besides being an avid Doom fan, also made some design decisions to keep Gorescript aligned with its inspiration source. Hand made levels, secret doors, the key card search and the 2.5D levels are some of the elements that became key features in Gorescript.

[img]http://media.indiedb.com/images/members/3/2595/2594235/profile/q8.png[/img]

The fast pace and the ever present danger in the game is meant to keep you on your feet and moving constantly. We wanted to make an equally satisfying game for people who like to clear levels and for people who like to speedrun while dodging everything the game throws at them. We’re glad our “run and gun, get killed and start again” recipe works :D.

We’ll leave you with one of the reviews that identifies another key design element, the trap doors that open up and reveal monsters, just when you thought you were safe.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=oK4RTO2Gojw

People have asked about the game’s story as well and judging by the speculations out there we could sum it up like this:

[b]You are trapped in a labyrinth in space and The Illuminati and some diabolical Pac-men (or Swedish meatballs) are out to get you.[/b]

In truth, Gorescript is a setting similar with some of the 80s movies that feature the inside of a computer game. It also draws its inspiration from titles such as [url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0087597/]The Last Starfighter[/url] and [url=http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0086014/?ref_=fn_al_tt_2]Nightmares[/url].

We’re so happy that our players and reviewers were spot on in identifying Gorescript’s elements and we’re extending our invitation to join the pixel horror filled maze.

[i]The Gorescript team[/i]

notes.title: First week on Steam
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/mgcjxlP.gif[/img]

It's been already a week since Gorescript launched on Steam guys. And what a blast this one has been!

Let me show to you some of the mentions we got on our first week (drumroll please!):

[h1]“...this is a classic-style FPS, but oh so much more deadlier, and presented with some charmingly enormous pixels.”
[url=https://www.rockpapershotgun.com/2017/06/16/gorescript-classic-fps-released/]RockPaperShorgun[/url]

“We've seen a few other classic FPSes on this list and Gorescript fits right at home among them, a lot of fun in its own right.”
[url=http://www.pcgamer.com/new-steam-games/]PC Gamer[/url]

“Keen understanding of both what made the arcade FPS of yesteryear great, and what could make it better: a rare homage in spirit over form.”
7/10 – [url=http://opnoobs.com/reviews/indie/fps/gorescript]OpNoobs[/url][/h1]

Cool huh? We are very excited that people actually "get" the game and move past the voxel wall. 

[b]Leaderboards time![/b] You know about our global leaderboard right? Time to cheer for the people that made it to the top of the world (excluding Sergiu (the creator of Gorescript) who probably cheated his way to the top).

[img]http://i.imgur.com/jCuKmFU.png[/img]

In the next week's update we will announce some awesome stuff that are coming (and when) in Gorescript. Till then,

[h1]Cheers & Stay tuned,
The Gorescript team[/h1]

notes.title: Hydras, Railguns & More
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/3XWcFaz.gif[/img]

[h1]Welcome to another week’s Gorescript update folks.[/h1]

- Did you notice the new railgun above? Definite power packed with killing satisfaction. We are going to be adding muzzle effects next weeks to maximise the usage pleasure of our weaponry. 

- We got a new member in the family. The Hydra. It’s not a boss (yeah! Of course, we will have those ones). Her multi-shooting heads will lead to some interesting fight techniques combined with the rest of the bad guys inventory. 

[img]http://i.imgur.com/n4iuKaB.gif[/img]
[img]http://i.imgur.com/PMRGmsi.png[/img]
What do you think? 

- Updated and better screenshots are also on their way to the store page.

---

Drum roll please! Now I would like to present to you a short interview with the creator of Gorescript’s soundtrack, Lawrence Steele of [url=http://satsu.ma]Satsuma Audio[/url] from UK. Enjoy:

[u][i]1.       Tell us some things about yourself.[/i][/u]

I am a composer and sound designer for games based in the north of England, I've been doing this for around 6 years now, with the last 3 or so it being my full-time job. I have always loved music and playing games so to combine the two to make a living is a dream come true! I decided to operate under the name 'Satsuma Audio' than just my name as I thought it would be more memorable and help me stand out a bit from the crowd.

[u][i]2.       Why did you choose to work on Gorescipt?[/i][/u]

I am a big fan of old school FPS games, Doom, Quake, Unreal etc. Me and my wife actually just finished playing through Doom 1 & 2 together, they are still awesome games even today! I thought gorescript was looking pretty great and the chance to write a full length 'dark electronic' OST sounded like a lot of fun!

[u][i]3.       How was your experience working with Gorescript?[/i][/u]

It has been really great actually, Sergiu (the game designer) has pretty much liked everything I've sent him straight away (this is not always the case in this job!) and I've been able to have a lot of creative freedom. I've tried to get a lot of different styles of electronic music in there, but still tried to keep it sounding like a cohesive whole.

[u][i]4.       How do you make sure the soundtrack fits the game?[/i][/u]

So to match the mood of the game I try to give all tracks a slightly dark, evil tinge to the music, to match the genre and the feeling of going through all these darkened rooms blasting monsters! I also try to find a balance between clean and crisp sounds to match the retro/neon visuals and distorted sounds to give a grungy, dark atmosphere to the music.

The idea is that it should blend into the background and allow the player to focus on the gameplay while simultaneously providing a sense of energy and pace at all times. I try to keep the tracks as varied as possible throughout, so as not to become too repetitive or boring when looped.

In the early stages of a new track I also have a video of the game playing on my 2nd monitor, just to make sure the music and the visuals 'gel' together well.

[u][i]5.       What did you enjoy the most when working on our game’s soundtrack?[/i][/u]

I work on quite a lot of slot machine apps, and more light, 'casual' stuff so it was great to have a chance to embrace my darker side and do something with more of an edge to it. It also gave me an excuse to bust out my hardware synths! 

I used an Arturia Minibrute and Moog Little Phatty throughout the soundtrack where suitable, they are both analogue synths and can help add an extra dimension to a track for sure.

[u][i]6.       Your top 3 favourite games you worked on:[/i][/u]

In no particular order...

[b]Gorescript[/b] - Not just saying this but it has been a lot of fun to work on and I'm pretty pleased with how it's turned out!

[b]WarBits[/b] - A turn-based strategy game for iOS, really polished well put together game, I wrote a retro/sci-fi-ish soundtrack for this as well as creating SFX and the end result turned out great I think.

[b]Tabletop Simulator[/b] - I made the SFX for this and it was interesting to work out how best to handle a physics based project such as this. Also, the game has really taken off in popularity since release which is awesome.

--- 

On another topic. As we are coming closer to the release of the game we would need all the available help we can get to show our game to the people that would love to play it. If you make videos on Youtube, you stream on Twitch, write game previews/reviews and you like Gorescript so far, let us know!

Cheers,
Gorescript

notes.title: Perfect Killing Music
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/Az3ePEm.gif[/img]
This weekly update on Gorescript will introduce the music of the game.
Just imagine the pixelated massacre with a proper soundtrack.

Nothing is more exhilarating than wiping out the hordes of voxel horrors in Gorescript than to do it on a soundtrack that fits. 

Gorescript soundtrack is well established in the techno and electronica genres and makes sure you're on your toes as you prepare to brave the levels.

This time we've got two specials from our soundtrack guaranteed to get you ready for this shooter and put you in the mood to play it.

[i]As you start the game you'll be greeted by this tune:[/i]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=SO5l1mfr5jQ

[i]And, as you roam through the levels, you'll definitely be knee deep in some pixel splatter on this song as well:[/i]
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EWgwl-2dF_w

Want to set the mood for action? You can find the soundtrack right here:
https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLDol1AveVopMhFPQDpYO5xRAGnh7mmw6i

notes.title: New alpha! New looks!
notes.notes:
[img]http://i.imgur.com/pPpYQLp.gif[/img]

Welcome to the weekly Gorescript update. We got some stuff to show you!

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/28498396/546d85ee1d12fd7ca2e4a5ca3474294cdddb8e6f.png[/img]

Did you notice anything different? What do you think?

Want a closer look to decide? Good news for you. Our free alpha just got an update with the new graphics. Download, give it a go and tell us what you think! (Ohh yeah, there is a new level in there as well).

Are you a Youtuber, or a Streamer, a reviewer, an extraterrestrial being of supreme power, all of the above? Would you like to show Gorescript to your audience? Let us know! 

[b]Keymailer:[/b] https://www.keymailer.co/g/games/40330
[b]Promoterapp:[/b] https://gorescript.promoterapp.com/pub/press

[h1]Free Alpha Patch notes:[/h1]

- A new level was added
- An option to show/hide the HUD (default is on; note that the HUD is always disabled on Masochistic difficulty regardless of this setting)
- An option to show/hide a timer for how much time you spent during your current level run (default is off) - Speedrunners delight!
- Increased the default mouse sensitivity to 0.35 (was 0.2); increased the maximum mouse sensitivity to 4 (was 1).
- Graphical improvements! Added normal maps to walls, floors and ceilings.
- Made a couple of changes to the blue key room in the first level for a smoother first-time experience.
- Added a score system. This score is cumulative across all levels (per save slot) and displayed whenever you complete a level.
- You can improve your score when replaying a certain level (using the "Level select" menu), either by collecting more random powerups (those marked with a question mark on the automap) or by completing the level in less than 3 minutes. Each second under 3 minutes will improve your score.
- Various small UI improvements.

[b]Have you played Gorescript? Here you go.[/b]

[url=http://www.amusedsloth.com/wp-content/uploads/9AiHNgvqGVsZ/gorescript-pre-alpha.zip]Gorescript free alpha direct download[/url]
